To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the installation of the optical cabling for the Tracker, ECAL, Pixel and DAQ systems was successfully completed.
the installation of the CMS optical cabling was completed on time and that the performance of the installed cabling meets the specifications of the system.
the CMS Tracker, the ECAL and the Pixel detector optical cabling systems were successfully installed, and that all optical channels were tested and verified to be operational.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optical properties of the optical links used in the CMS Tracker, the ECAL, the Pixel detectors, and in the Data Acquisition System.
the design, installation and testing of the optical fibre cabling for the Tracker, ECAL, Pixel and other CMS subsystems, including the optical links for the CMS Data Acquisition.
the design of a new optical fibre cable for the LHC experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optical cabling for CMS is now fully functional and ready for use.
the optical cabling system is working as designed and has performed very well during installation and commissioning.
all of the CMS Tracker optical cables have been tested, installed and commissioned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optical cabling system is working as designed.
the optical cabling system is now ready for the CMS physics programme.
it is possible to achieve an optical link failure rate below 1% in a large system of this kind.
The main takeaway from our work is that
optical cabling is robust and reliable and that the optical time-domain reflectometers are a very useful tool in the installation of optical cables.
optical cabling installation, testing and troubleshooting is an essential component of detector installation, and that a dedicated team is necessary to carry out the work efficiently.

a large scale optical cabling project of this type can be successfully carried out, and the lessons learnt will be useful in the future for the LHCb upgrade, and for the LHC Phase 1 and Phase 2 upgrades.
